content.thinking: The rollout of the monthly-spend-feature flag at 23:47, going from 110 off to 90 on, lines up exactly with the onset of the p99 spike, while the change record timestamp was just logged later at alert time — and there were no deploys involved, so this flag toggle looks like the real trigger.

hypotheses.subject: monthly-spend-feature
hypotheses.summary: The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was rolled out from off to on; the first minute with any 'on' evaluations (23:47) is exactly the first minute p99 latency departs baseline (199ms → 390ms, then 1300-1700ms as the rollout completed to 100% on). No code or config deploy occurred in the preceding 24 hours.

supporting_evidence.claim: Every recorded change to io-shop from 2026-09-21T23:47:00Z to 2026-09-22T23:47:00Z. (nothing changed in this window)

hypotheses.summary: Alternative: the latency arriving through the newly enabled code path is actually a slow dependency that the monthly-spend feature calls (the flag merely exposed it). The logs name no upstream service and show no timeout/5xx errors, so this is unsupported but would explain multi-second p99 with flat error rate and flat request volume.

supporting_evidence.claim: p99 1326-1702ms with error_rate unchanged (0.005-0.02) and request_volume flat at 1200 - latency-only degradation typical of a slow downstream call
Only error lines present are 'ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection', which predate the onset and name no dependency
